title: Publish offline chart tarballs with sha256 checksums for signed Private bundles
author: Devon Price
release_notes: Private/on-prem offline bundle pipeline can now consume published chart tarballs and verify their sha256 hashes from a generated checksums file (referenced by the signed bundle manifest).
body: Summary: Adds a deterministic packaging step for Redwood Helm charts intended for Redwood Private offline bundles. The pipeline now produces versioned chart tarballs (.tgz) for each supported chart and emits a sha256 checksums file that can be referenced by the signed offline bundle manifest. Motivation: For air-gapped installs, we need to transport a complete set of Helm charts without relying on remote chart repos. Bundle signing (separate work in the installer/release pipeline) needs stable inputs: a predictable chart archive name + a hash file that can be included in the bundle manifest and signed. This PR does NOT implement signing here; it only produces the chart artifacts and checksum outputs in a stable layout for the release tooling to ingest. Key changes: (1) New make target `make package-offline` that runs `helm dependency build` with pinned versions, packages charts to `dist/offline-charts/<channel>/<version>/`, and writes `checksums-sha256.txt` in the same directory. (2) Standardized archive naming: `<chartName>-<chartVersion>.tgz` (no build metadata). (3) Deterministic packaging: sets `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` (when present) and normalizes file ordering before hashing to reduce drift across runs; also ensures `Chart.lock` is generated and included in the packaged chart. (4) Adds CI job `offline-chart-artifacts` that runs packaging and verifies that rerunning packaging yields identical checksums within the same commit (best-effort determinism check; see notes). (5) Documentation: updates `RELEASING.md` with the offline artifact path conventions and how the signing/manifest tooling should reference the output. Output format: `dist/offline-charts/private/<appVersion>/` contains `redwood-private-<chartVersion>.tgz`, `redwood-runtime-<chartVersion>.tgz`, `redwood-observability-<chartVersion>.tgz`, plus `checksums-sha256.txt`. The checksums file uses one entry per line: `<sha256>  <filename>` (two spaces) to match common tooling (`sha256sum -c`). Example: `8d2b2a6c9b0f5d2bb8e1c7f2e7bb8f1d74b6b9b3f71a4f5cd2d2f7b1c4a9f3d2  redwood-private-1.18.0.tgz`. Notes / determinism constraints: Helm chart packaging can still drift if dependencies pull non-deterministic archives or if the local environment injects timestamps. We mitigate most of this by requiring dependencies to be pinned, generating `Chart.lock`, and hashing the final tarballs. CI checks that the checksum file remains stable on a second packaging pass in the same runner. If we see drift across runners, release tooling should treat the checksums as the source of truth for a given build id and record the build provenance in the signed bundle manifest (tracked in ENG-4822/installer work). Files/areas changed (high-level): `.github/workflows/offline-chart-artifacts.yml` (new CI job), `Makefile` (new packaging targets), `scripts/package_offline_charts.sh` (new; creates dist layout and checksums), `charts/*/Chart.yaml` (minor alignment + ensure dependencies are pinned), `RELEASING.md` (offline artifact conventions). Commits: 1) chore(ci): add workflow to build offline chart artifacts and upload as build artifact 2) build: add package-offline target + packaging script 3) build: generate checksums-sha256.txt and validate via sha256sum -c 4) docs: update releasing guide with offline bundle chart artifact layout Review conversation: Connor O'Brien: Can we guarantee the output paths match what the Private bundle manifest generator expects? Devon Price: Added explicit directory layout in RELEASING.md and aligned with the current bundle tooling draft; also added env vars `OFFLINE_CHART_CHANNEL` + `OFFLINE_CHART_VERSION` so release tooling can control the exact destination. Connor O'Brien: Please ensure the checksum file format is compatible with `sha256sum -c` on minimal distros. Devon Price: Updated to two-space separator; added a CI smoke check using `sha256sum -c checksums-sha256.txt`. Sahana Iyer: The determinism check is good, but can we fail if `helm dependency update` runs? We shouldn’t be updating dependencies during packaging. Devon Price: Packaging script now uses `helm dependency build` and errors if `Chart.lock` would change (git diff check). Jordan Lee: Please add an example stanza for how the manifest should reference these outputs (relative paths). Devon Price: Added a short example in RELEASING.md showing `charts/redwood-private-<ver>.tgz` and `charts/checksums-sha256.txt` entries as inputs to the manifest builder. Ethan Park: Any risk to existing online chart publishing? Devon Price: No changes to chart repo publishing; this is additive and only runs in the new CI workflow and release tooling. CI: build/lint (pass), chart lint (pass), offline-chart-artifacts (pass), determinism re-run check (pass). Merge: Squash merged by Connor O'Brien after approvals. Follow-ups: ENG-4828 will wire these artifacts into the offline bundle builder; installer PRs will verify hashes from the signed manifest during preflight.
